prompt: Which course in the track teaches equivalence partitioning and boundary values?

choices.text: testing-cicd
choices.why: That course is about running tests in a pipeline.

choices.text: web-automation
choices.why: That one automates a browser; choosing the cases comes first.

choices.text: manual-testing
choices.why: Right: the next course in the track, and the one that requires this one.

choices.text: qa-fundamentals, in its lessons on black-box testing
choices.why: Lesson 6 names those techniques and leaves them to the next course.

prompt: At Cine Aurora, who decides what the ticket shop does and writes its rules down?

choices.text: Lia, who tests them
choices.why: Lia checks the rules and questions them; she does not own them.

choices.text: Joana
choices.why: Right: she is the product owner.

choices.text: Célia, who has sold tickets for twenty years
choices.why: Célia knows every rule, and runs the box office; she does not write the shop’s rules.

choices.text: Rafael, since he wrote the code that applies them
choices.why: He turns the rules into code, which is where a reading of a rule becomes a decision.

prompt: What does quality assurance look at, in the sense this lesson uses?

choices.text: The process: how the work gets done
choices.why: Right: assurance is process-oriented and preventive.

choices.text: The product, once there is a product to examine
choices.why: That is quality control, the detecting half.

choices.text: The test results
choices.why: Results are what detection produces; assurance works before there are any.

choices.text: The customers’ complaints after release
choices.why: Those are the latest evidence there is, and still evidence about the product.

prompt: A team reads every new requirement aloud and asks, for each sentence, whether it could mean two things. What is this?

choices.text: Dynamic testing, because the team is examining something
choices.why: Dynamic means the program runs; here there is no program yet.

choices.text: Quality control of the product
choices.why: There is no product yet; it is the plan being examined.

choices.text: Detection, since a defect in the sentence is being found
choices.why: The ambiguity is found, and the defect in the code never happens: that is prevention.

choices.text: Static testing, and prevention
choices.why: Right: nothing runs, and the defect is stopped before it is written.

prompt: Dijkstra said testing can show the presence of defects, never their absence. What follows for a tester?
hint: Four correct answers, and a fifth input.

choices.text: Testing is pointless, so prevention should replace it
choices.why: Prevention cannot catch what nobody thought to ask; the two feed each other.

choices.text: Enough passing tests eventually prove a program correct
choices.why: That is exactly what the sentence denies.

choices.text: Only automated tests prove absence, because they run thousands of inputs
choices.why: Automation runs more inputs, and still only the inputs it runs.

choices.text: Choosing the inputs is the skill
choices.why: Right: that is why lessons 6, 19 and 20 are about choosing.

prompt: After the sixty-year-old’s ticket, the team fixes `age > 60`. In the terms of this lesson, what has not been done yet?
hint: One defect, or a class of them?

choices.text: Detection, since the code has only been corrected
choices.why: Detection already happened: that is how the defect was found.

choices.text: A second test of the same age, run after the fix to confirm it holds
choices.why: Re-running the check confirms the fix; it does not stop the next ambiguous sentence.

choices.text: Nothing: the defect is repaired, so quality is assured
choices.why: The cause, words that allow two readings, is still there.

choices.text: Asking why the sentence made it possible
choices.why: Right: fixing the code repairs one defect; changing the process repairs a class.

prompt: Match each activity to the half of quality assurance it belongs to, and whether anything runs.

pairs.left: running a program with chosen inputs
adopting a rule after a defect
pairs.right: prevention of the same kind of defect

prompt: Which path to a lab does this course recommend?
hint: It costs the least and changes nothing else.

choices.text: Installed on the computer you already use
choices.why: Right: a directory and a virtual environment, nothing running in the background.

choices.text: A virtual machine with Ubuntu 24.04
choices.why: A good path if you would rather not touch your own system; it costs gigabytes, and it is the second choice.

choices.text: An online machine such as GitHub Codespaces
choices.why: It works, on a free allowance its owner can change; the course does not depend on it.

choices.text: A lab the platform provides
choices.why: The platform runs nothing for you: the lab is yours.

prompt: Why is behave installed inside `~/aurora/.venv` rather than for the whole system?

choices.text: To make it faster
choices.why: A virtual environment changes where packages live, not how fast they run.

choices.text: So the lab is one directory that changes nothing else and is thrown away whole
choices.why: Right: deleting `~/aurora` removes every trace of the course.

choices.text: Because behave refuses to run outside a virtual environment
choices.why: It would run anywhere; the environment is about keeping the computer clean.

choices.text: Because the system Python is too old for it
choices.why: The environment uses the system’s Python; it only keeps the packages apart.

prompt: How many megabytes did `~/aurora/.venv` take on the recording machine?
Before `pip` installs into the environment in a new terminal, the environment has to be ___.
In a new terminal, `python3 -c "import behave"` answers `ModuleNotFoundError`, although the setup finished. What is the likeliest cause?

choices.text: behave 1.3.3 does not exist
choices.why: It exists; the failure for a missing version comes from `pip`, with a list.

choices.text: The environment is not active in that terminal
choices.why: Right: the system’s Python has never heard of behave.

choices.text: The installation failed without saying so, and has to be redone from the start
choices.why: Activating the environment makes the same line work; nothing has to be reinstalled.

choices.text: `python3-venv` is missing, so pip installed behave nowhere
choices.why: Without it the environment would never have been created at all.

prompt: `pip install behave==1.3.9` fails with a list of versions. What is that list for?
hint: Compare what you asked for with what exists.

choices.text: It is noise, and only the last line matters
choices.why: Here the list is the part that tells you what to type.

choices.text: It shows what exists, so a mistyped version is visible at a glance
choices.why: Right: 1.3.9 is not in it and 1.3.3 is.

choices.text: It lists the versions already installed
choices.why: It lists what the package index offers, installed or not.

choices.text: It is the order in which pip will try them
choices.why: pip tries nothing else: the exact version was asked for.

prompt: A setup error prints twenty lines. Which one do you read first?

choices.text: None: reinstall first, then read
choices.why: Evidence is read before guessing.

choices.text: The first error
choices.why: Right: the lines after it are usually its consequences.

choices.text: The last line, always, because it sums the rest up
choices.why: The last line is what to search for; the first error is what to understand.

choices.text: Whichever line mentions your file
choices.why: Your file may appear only as a consequence.

prompt: What does `python tickets.py 60 no thu 20:00` print, and what should it print by the rule?
hint: Run the edges of the age.

choices.text: R$ 36,00, and it should be R$ 18,00
choices.why: Right: sixty pays full price, one year short of the half-price ticket.

choices.text: R$ 18,00, which is correct
choices.why: That is what sixty-one gets.

choices.text: R$ 14,00, and it should be R$ 18,00
choices.why: R$ 14,00 is a half-price matinée.

choices.text: An error, because the age is out of range
choices.why: The program prints a price for any whole number.

prompt: Where was the sixty-year-old’s defect first, before it was in `tickets.py`?

choices.text: In the requirement, whose words allowed two readings
choices.why: Right: "over-60s" can include sixty or not.

choices.text: In Rafael’s carelessness
choices.why: His reading was reasonable; the sentence allowed it. Lesson 18 is about asking why, not who.

choices.text: In the law, which changed after the rule was written
choices.why: The law grants the half price from sixty, and the box office always sold it that way.

choices.text: Nowhere: it appeared when the program ran
choices.why: Running exposed it; it was written before.

prompt: Lia’s first four runs all agreed with the rule. Why did she keep going?
hint: What do four agreeing answers say about the fifth input?

choices.text: A test has to fail before it counts
choices.why: A passing test counts; it just says less than people think.

choices.text: Four agreeing answers say nothing about untried inputs
choices.why: Right: the rule names three ages, and an edge is where a reading differs.

choices.text: Four is below the minimum number of tests a release needs
choices.why: There is no such number; the choice of input mattered, not the count.

choices.text: She suspected Rafael
choices.why: Doubt is about the program and the sentence, not a person; lesson 4 makes that distinction.

prompt: A team prides itself on catching every defect in its test stage, and fixes each one fast. Nothing about how it writes requirements has changed in two years. What is it missing?

choices.text: Prevention, the half that learns from each defect
choices.why: Right: it pays for every mistake twice and never asks why it was possible.

choices.text: More testers in the test stage, so that defects are found sooner
choices.why: More detection finds more of the same defects, later and at the same cost.

choices.text: Nothing, if no defect escapes
choices.why: Even caught in time, every defect cost the making and the finding.

choices.text: Dynamic testing
choices.why: That is the half it already does.
